title: Rethinking Efficient Graph Coarsening via a Non-Selfishness Principle
claim: Local, neighborhood-aware merging preserves graph structure better than greedy pairwise merging, so the coarsened graph's structural measures drift less.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared x-axis, red vs blue curves
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the same x-axis, Merge Round, running from 0 to about 2.2×10^3. The left plot shows Dirichlet Energy (×10^3) falling steadily from about 4.2 to under 1. Selfish Merging is a red solid line and Non-selfish Merging is a blue solid line. The two curves start together, then the red line drops faster and ends lower. The right plot shows Average Edge Betweenness Centrality (×10^-3) as dashed lines. Both curves rise from about 0.83 to a peak near 1.1 and then fall. The red curve peaks higher and rebounds at the end, while the blue curve stays smoother and lower. A legend sits in the top corner of each panel. Red marks the baseline and blue marks the proposed approach.
caption: The changes of Dirichlet Energy and Average Edge Betweenness Centrality in the coarsened graphs based on selfishness and non-selfishness coarsening strategies.
abstract: Graph coarsening is a graph dimensionality reduction technique that aims to construct a smaller and more tractable graph while preserving the essential structural and semantic properties of the original graph. However, most existing methods rely on pair-wise similarity matching, where each node independently searches for its best partner based on global information. This selfishness matching paradigm incurs substantial computational and memory overhead. To address this problem, we shift to a non-selfishness principle that prioritizes the collective interference of neighborhood in coarsening, and propose an efficient method named NOPE, which achieves linear memory consumption and near-linear computational complexity in the number of nodes. Furthermore, we derive a faster variant NOPE*, which reduces O(Î´\dot d) interference evaluation to O(d) based on the local isotropy assumption, and consequently alleviates the computational bottleneck for high-degree nodes. Experimental results show that NOPE* achieves 1.8-10\times speedup over NOPE and surpass almost all baselines with 1-3 orders of magnitude acceleration. Meanwhile, learning on coarsened graphs yields comparable performance to original graphs, and can even show superior performance over LLM-based graph reasoning owing to compact graph information. The code can be available at https://github.com/dazonglian/NOPE-main.
